messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: ideas for future stan development
parts:
Hi,

As many of us I have started my travel to stan starting with WinBUGS.  I found stan modeling environment quite flexible.  I wonder if it makes sense to implement in stan sampling algorithms such as Gibbs sampling, Generalized Direct Sampling.  In additional to sampling based algorithms implementation of deterministic algorithms such as Expectation Propagation might be useful.  Specifically, at Purdue University, we have developed an algorithm based on KL optimization. Many of those algorithms require likelihood function which may become a nasty looking function if you try to code in R.  A common modeling language framework as well as diversity of algorithms would be great.

Another idea is to remove PK modeling gap.  While WinBUGS has PKBugs for PK modeling, stan currently doesn't have this capability. I know that there are some thoughts but it would be nice to have this capability sooner.

Thanks,
Linas

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] ideas for future stan development
parts: You are so in luck. See below.

On Sep 3, 2014, at 1:36 PM, Linas Mockus <linasm...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi,
>
> As many of us I have started my travel to stan starting with WinBUGS. I found stan modeling environment quite flexible. I wonder if it makes sense to implement in stan sampling algorithms such as Gibbs sampling, Generalized Direct Sampling. In additional to sampling based algorithms implementation of deterministic algorithms such as Expectation Propagation might be useful. Specifically, at Purdue University, we have developed an algorithm based on KL optimization. Many of those algorithms require likelihood function which may become a nasty looking function if you try to code in R. A common modeling language framework as well as diversity of algorithms would be great.

We are actively working on all three of marginal maximum likelihood,
expectation propagation and variational inference. Variational will
probably be the first one done. It's being taken on by Alp Kucukelbir
(a post-doc working with Dave Blei).

We're also working on plain old maximum likelihood so that we can
recreate the lm() and glm() functionality in R. Andrew's sketched out
the design and it should all be wrapped up for Stan 2.6. Early
performance testing with our L-BFGS optimizer is promising.

All of these depend on Laplace approximations, which in turn depend on
the just-finished higher-order autodiff, which will be out in Stan 2.5.
(That'll also pave the way for Riemannian manifold HMC, which is
prototyped and has just been awaiting higher-order autodiff being done;
we're also working on speeding up higher-order autodiff.)

> Another idea is to remove PK modeling gap. While WinBUGS has PKBugs for PK modeling, stan currently doesn't have this capability. I know that there are some thoughts but it would be nice to have this capability sooner.
>

You should see the first version for non-stiff equations in
Stan 2.5! The final draft version is currently unit testing
in my other window. It was a pretty substantial effort because
we need derivatives of the solutions in order to do HMC and
gradient-based optimization.

We also have plans to write wrappers for PK/PD applications in
particular. Here's a link to a PK/PD project we did with Novartis on
a prototype implementation directly in C++ coupled with some nifty
meta-analysis:

http://www.page-meeting.org/?abstract=3200

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] ideas for future stan development
parts:
I'd think you'd be better off with custom EP or VB
implementations for specific models. We're going to have
to approximate. And EP and VB are still in the research
stages --- we have no idea how well the "black box" methods
will work. They're going to reply on some pretty crude
Laplace approximations.

And even if we do eventually come up with something more
general, I think the applications are still interesting (stamping
out pills!).

- Bob
